output.brief: Store 14's rise is based on interim estimates extrapolated from partial cycle counts. The analytics memo says those estimates are only accurate to about ±0.6 points a quarter. Of past stores showing two straight rises of this size, only about half were confirmed by the year-end count. Store 14's own full counts have been steady at 1.5–1.8%. So it's unclear whether real losses have risen. Self-checkout, customer theft and staff theft are all still open. The self-checkout case rests on timing and trade articles. The rise in recorded shoplifting incidents matches a chain-wide jump after the new incident app launched in April, while chain shrink stayed flat. The ethics-line tip was checked on CCTV and found to be routine cardboard runs. Sales mix didn't change, so it doesn't explain the rise. Two neighbouring stores without self-checkout showed no rise, which is only weak evidence. Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and refuse the proposal to drop it. Hold off on pulling the self-checkout lanes, hiring a guard, or suspending the night stocker until the count result is compared with the interim figures. Confidence is moderate.
